In today's digital world, finding genuine relationships is tougher than ever. At Hinge, we’re on a mission to inspire intimate connection to create a less lonely world. Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
We are looking for a Senior UX Researcher to join our Design Research team, embedded in the Human Care mission. Human Care is where Oura expands beyond tracking into territory with real clinical stakes — products that help members understand and act on their health, connect to care when they need it, and generate evidence that Oura can drive meaningful outcomes.
In this role, you will represent the voice of the user for a mission that sits at the intersection of consumer experience and healthcare. You'll uncover the deep user insights that shape how we build — partnering closely with product managers, designers, and clinical scientists to ensure we're solving the right problems in the right ways with deep appreciation for the nuance and care our members require.
This is a hybrid-remote role, with the expectation to work from our San Francisco offices at least half-time.

Lead user research for the software team connecting members to healthcare partners. Plan, conduct, and analyze a range of user research studies, including ethnographic studies, contextual inquiries, user interviews, surveys, and diary studies to gather both qualitative and quantitative data.
Bring clinical and regulatory context into product decisions — understanding how FDA-regulated features, HIPAA consent flows, and EHR integrations shape what's possible and what's appropriate for members.
Develop research-backed frameworks for how Oura surfaces clinical-grade data (biomarkers, lab results, risk signals) to consumer audiences in a way that's clear, actionable, and emotionally resonant — not alarming.
Partner with the clinical and health science teams to ensure research bridges behavioral and physiological insight — understanding not just what users do but what health context drives those behaviors.
Build and maintain a longitudinal view of our members from the lens of connected care— their motivations, anxieties, health literacy, and relationship with clinical care — that informs roadmap prioritization.
What You Likely Have
Experience: 5+ years of professional UX research experience, with meaningful work at the intersection of consumer product and healthcare, digital health, or clinical technology.
Research Expertise: Demonstrated ability to research complex, high-stakes experiences — medical devices, clinical software, diagnostic tools, telehealth, or patient-facing health apps — where decisions have real consequences.
Technical Acumen: Deep understanding of health literacy variation across populations and how to design research that accounts for members ranging from highly health-engaged to newly diagnosed to clinical-care-avoidant.
Domain Awareness: Experience navigating regulated or compliance-sensitive environments (HIPAA, FDA, IRB) and understanding how those constraints shape research design and product decisions.
Problem-Solving: Strong point of view on how to make clinical data legible and meaningful to non-clinical audiences — you've wrestled with the problem of surfacing biomarkers, risk indicators, or diagnostic signals without inducing unnecessary anxiety or oversimplification.
Collaboration: Proven experience working in cross-functional teams including PMs, clinicians, designers, data scientists, and commercial teams. You know how to translate research into the language each stakeholder acts on.
Can-do attitude: You can operate independently across multiple concurrent workstreams, prioritize ruthlessly, and build a research program that is respected..

Experience researching connected care or care coordination products — understanding how data moves between patients, wearables, and clinical workflows, and where friction emerges in that loop.
Familiarity with metabolic health, GLP-1 medications, or cardiometabolic care pathways as a research subject area.
Prior work with B2B healthcare products — enterprise dashboards, clinical decision support, payer or health system tools — where the research audience includes clinical administrators, researchers, or care teams in addition to end users.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

UX research at Anthropic works across products used by millions of people, on interactions that don't have established conventions yet. We inform critical decisions through rigorous research, working closely with curious, open-minded stakeholders who are eager to learn along with us.

We combine qualitative and quantitative methods to understand user needs in a space that's evolving faster than anyone can track. We move fast, favor impact over polish, and increasingly build our own tools, deeply leveraging Claude to do research at the speed and rigor this environment demands.
This role is on the Platform research team, embedded in Anthropic's Platform organization, which comprises the API, the agent and connector infrastructure developers build on top of it, and the Console, SDKs, and documentation they use to do it. A large share of what gets built with Claude is built on this platform, including many of Anthropic's own products, and the people who use it range from individual developers to the largest enterprises.
The teams that build the platform are deeply technical, move quickly, and are deeply curious about and engaged with users. User research's job here is to give them a deeper and more systematic understanding of those users than they can get on their own, and to help the organization decide what to build for them next.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with a great deal of autonomy. You'll work with the rest of the Platform user research team and with Platform's leaders to decide where research can make the biggest difference, and then lead that work yourself.

Work with Platform's leaders and teams to understand what they most need to know about the people building on Claude, decide what is and isn't worth studying, and own that agenda
Design and run the research yourself using both qualitative and quantitative methods
Study the full range of people the platform serves: developers, the teams and companies building products on it, and the people who administer and buy it
Communicate findings to product managers, designers, and engineers and follow them through to product decisions, while building the shared understanding of users that lets teams make good calls on their own
Build the tools and infrastructure that let research keep pace with the platform, using Claude heavily and inventing methods where the existing ones don't fit

Industry UX research experience independently scoping, designing, running, and reporting end-to-end studies
Mixed-methods expertise: interviewing technical users well, and designing and analyzing surveys rigorously
A technical background, in one of these forms: you've worked as a software engineer; you have a sustained body of developer-experience research on APIs, SDKs, or developer tools; or you have a sustained track record of researching deeply technical products. In practice: you can read our documentation, build something small on the platform, and keep up with very technical teams without translation
Hands-on use of AI in your own research: you already run your work through it and use it to build your own analyses and tooling

8+ years of industry UX research experience
Experience setting the research strategy for a product or product area, with a track record of research that changed direction at the strategy level, not just the feature level, in direct partnership with product or organization leaders
Experience embedding with engineering-led product teams that ship fast and earning influence there, from the engineer who owns the endpoint up to the head of the organization

Experience building with AI yourself using coding tools and agents, and an appetite to help build the research tools that don't exist yet
Experience researching pricing, packaging, or how customers decide what a product is worth, especially for usage-based or developer products
Background in API-ecosystem or developer-platform research

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Healthcare is complicated: people are anxious about their health, insurance coverage is obscure, and there’s uncertainty in finding the right type of care. Meanwhile, providers face thin margins, growing competition, and operational workflows that drown their staff in administrative burden.

As a Principal UX Researcher, you'll immerse yourself deeply in understanding these problems, and own the research strategy for one of Zocdoc's two core user groups: the patients searching for care, or the practices delivering it.
You'll report to the Director of Research and partner with Product, Design, Brand, Marketing, and Data Science leadership to proactively shape product strategy. You'll set the bar for high quality strategic quantitative and qualitative research that cuts across product teams and shapes the product roadmap. You'll identify unanswered research questions and unvalidated assumptions across the company, develop a clear POV on user needs, and use research insights to drive business objectives.

s.h: Your work will span three connected areas
s.t:
Define who we're building for, and what they're trying to get done. You'll use a mixed-methods toolset to map the jobs, needs, and mindsets of our users, helping product, marketing, and sales teams see which needs matter most and how they differ meaningfully across groups.
Shape high-ambiguity problem spaces with qualitative and quantitative evidence. You'll lead research for zero-to-one opportunities where there's little precedent and limited data. You'll help teams define the problem, test the assumptions underneath a proposed solution, evaluate concepts at scale, and decide what is worth building before a roadmap hardens around an answer.
Measure the user experience. Help product teams understand how well our products actually meet user needs. That means partnering with Data Science to define user-centered metrics, then standing up survey programs and tracking that make them measurable over time.
You’ll enjoy this role if you are…
Personally motivated by being a positive change agent in the world and want to dive into solving complex social problems
Energized by working across qual and quant
Experienced working on cross-functional learning agendas with marketing and data science teams
Driven to make the case for human-centred constructs in a data-driven organization
Comfortable with full research domain ownership for your product space
Motivated not just to continuously experiment with new AI tools and processes, but to help build sustainable agentic infrastructure that can scale across teams

Owning the research agenda for your audience, and scope and execute complex, multi-phase studies from early strategy through launch and iteration
Designing and fielding quantitative research (including needs sizing, concept testing, and tracking), as well as own the sampling strategy for hard to reach populations
Combining behavioral data with qualitative signal so teams understand not just where people drop off, but what they came to do and whether they got it
Evolving our measurement program (tracking surveys, benchmarking, longitudinal and diary studies, continuous discovery) that holds the business accountable to user outcomes rather than proxy metrics
Packaging old and new insights from diverse studies into memorable frameworks that are usable by diverse audiences
Partnering beyond Product with Marketing, Brand, and Sales, so that one shared view of the user shapes positioning and go-to-market as well as the product roadmap
Building and evolving new research systems that reduce one-off reactive research
Mentoring junior researchers and bringing industry knowledge and expertise to our practice
Representing UXR on business unit leadership teams

Experience defining measurement, not just consuming it: a tracking program, a benchmark, a segmentation, or a metric that a business actually adopted
The ability to build and leverage research infrastructure including external sample, agencies, and contractor partners, as well as make a case for the budget behind them
Depth in either consumer products at scale or B2B and SaaS products with complex, multi-stakeholder adoption
Experience leading foundational, cross-functional research efforts, partnering with Data Science and Marketing as peers rather than as service providers
Superb communication skills. You believe in keeping all of your stakeholders in the loop and know that multiple mediums of communication are the key to success
A track record of influencing leaders who lack experience working with research
Capability to zoom out to systems-level strategy and zoom in to execution details, and are comfortable navigating ambiguity and political nuance along the way
